In [[mathematics]], a '''Hodge algebra''' or '''algebra with straightening law''' is a [[commutative algebra]] that is a [[free module]] over some [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] ''R'', together with a given basis similar to the basis of [[standard monomial]]s of the [[coordinate ring]] of a [[Grassmannian]]. Hodge algebras were introduced by {{harvs|txt| last1=De Concini | first1=Corrado | authorlink1=Corrado De Concini| last2=Eisenbud | first2=David | author2-link=David Eisenbud | last3=Procesi | first3=Claudio | authorlink3= Claudio Procesi| title=Hodge algebras | publisher=[[Société Mathématique de France]] | location=Paris | series=Astérisque |mr=680936 | year=1982 | volume=91}}, who named them after [[W. V. D. Hodge]].
